feedback.Physical Object: Excluded — This is an abstract logical structure, not a physical entity.
feedback.Synthetic: Included — Constructed and formulated by humans.
feedback.Biological/Biomimetic: Excluded — Not derived from biological systems.
feedback.Powered: Excluded — Not energy-dependent in abstract form.
feedback.Observable: Excluded — Not directly perceivable without representation.
feedback.Physical Medium: Excluded — Not defined by material composition.
feedback.Active: Excluded — Passive until implemented within a system.
feedback.Intentionally Designed: Excluded — Represents logical inference, but not a functional artifact.
feedback.Outputs Effect: Excluded — Requires implementation to affect external conditions.
feedback.Processes Signals/Logic: Excluded — It defines logical behavior but does not perform computation itself.
feedback.State-Transforming: Excluded — Describes transformation conditions, but does not enact them.
feedback.Human-Interactive: Excluded — Not inherently interactive without embodiment.
feedback.System-integrated: Excluded — Can be used in systems but not inherently part of one.
feedback.Functionally Autonomous: Excluded — Cannot act on its own.
feedback.System-Essential: Excluded — Not indispensable to any single system.
feedback.Symbolic: Included — Encodes inference via symbolic representation.
feedback.Compositional: Included — Constructed from logical parts (conditions, consequences).
feedback.Normative: Included — Directs expected behavior within logical/machine systems.
feedback.Meta: Included — Can describe rules about rules or logic structures themselves.
feedback.Temporal: Included — May define behavior conditioned by time-based triggers or sequences.
feedback.Social Construct: Included — Logical rules are agreed upon by intellectual communities.
feedback.Institutionally Defined: Included — Used and taught within formal domains like math, law, and programming.
feedback.Identity-Linked: Excluded — Not tied to individual or group identity.
feedback.Regulated: Included — Standardized in formal logic systems and programming languages.
feedback.Economically Significant: Included — Drives logic in systems with massive economic consequences.
feedback.Politicised: Included — Embedded in debates about algorithmic governance and transparency.
feedback.Ritualised: Included — Appears in structured instructional, testing, and formal processes.
feedback.Ethically Significant: Included — Conditional logic plays a key role in ethical algorithms and decision frameworks.

encoding_notes: This encoding frames the 'If-Then' rule as a foundational logical structure with symbolic, normative, and social meaning. Though inert by itself, it is central to rule-based computation and governance logic.
